messages.subject: Starting Rattle Every Time
parts:
Hi,

I installed R version 3.1.1 and the all necessary files for Rattle 3.0 Wednesday 8/20/2014 and played around with Rattle to test drive it.  Everything was  ok so I ordered the Rattle book from Amazon.com to learn Rattle better.  But the following day when I opened R and tried to run Rattle by typing > library(rattle) I got the message: Error in library(rattle) : there is no package called 'rattle'.  I even enclosed rattle in double quotes to see if that was the problem and still got the same error message.  This is my first time of using Rattle. Having earlier installed "RGtk2" I don't think I need to install it again on my Windows 7 machine each time I want to start Rattle.

So what am I doing wrong, and what different procedure should I follow every time I want to start Rattle?  I will appreciate any help, please.  Thanks.

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: Starting Rattle Every Time
parts:
That's an odd problem - you certainly should not have to install packages multiple times.

Perhaps try installing rattle again:

> install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com", type="source")

then reboot and ensure it is still available. If not, there must be some system configuration issue?

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com

messages.subject: Re: Starting Rattle Every Time
parts:
Thanks Williams for your speed reply.

After submitting my post, I went back and re-installed Rattle and started Rattle to further explore it before I went to bed.  After reading your reply, I opened R, and started Rattle by typing this: > library(rattle) and then > rattle(). Voila!
Rattle started as expected. I can't wait for my Rattle book to arrive next week so I can immerse myself in learning Rattle. Thanks a million.

CK
